transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Um, hi. I guess I came in because... well, I just keep feeling like I’ve completely let my family down by taking on this mortgage. It's just hanging over me. The house is okay, I mean, it has this really big oak tree in the front yard, but the roots are starting to crack the driveway. I was reading online that you can hire an arborist, but they charge like three hundred dollars just to come out and look at it. I took a couple botany classes back when I was in college, so I thought maybe I could figure out if the roots were rotting or something, but... I don't know, I couldn't tell. 

But yeah, the mortgage just makes me feel so guilty all the time. And then at work—I wait tables—every small mistake I make just proves to me that I’m completely useless. Like if I forget to bring a side of ranch or mix up a drink order, it just hits me that I deserve whatever bad stuff happens to me. The other day a guy left his tip entirely in nickels and dimes, and I just stood there at the booth thinking about how I can't seem to do anything right.
How long have you been feeling this guilty and worthless?

Well, I guess... the really bad periods, where I just feel so depressed and guilty about everything, that's been going on for about a year and two months now. It just sort of settled in around then. That was right around the time my sister got a new car, actually. It was a Honda Civic, one of those silver ones. She got a really good deal on it because the dealership was trying to clear out the previous year's models. I remember she was so excited, she drove it all the way over to my place just to show me the backup camera. I tried to act happy for her, but I just kept thinking about how I could never afford something like that, especially with the mortgage. And then I started worrying that the oak tree in my yard was going to drop a branch on her new car while it was parked in the driveway. I actually went out and moved my own car to the street just in case, which meant I had to park under this streetlamp that flickers all night. It’s really annoying, it’s like a strobe light in my bedroom window... but yeah, about fourteen months of feeling like this.
During these fourteen months, have you lost interest in or pleasure from activities you usually enjoy?

Um, lost interest? I mean, I guess I haven't really noticed that happening. I still do the things I normally do, like... well, I still try to read. I was actually reading this article the other day about how they’re changing the recipe for that one brand of ginger ale. The one with the green label? Apparently, there was this whole lawsuit because they weren't using real ginger, or maybe they were using real ginger but not enough of it to legally call it ginger ale. I don't know, it seems like everything is just corn syrup now anyway. I used to drink it a lot when I was a kid whenever I got an upset stomach. My mom swore by it. She’d always make me drink it flat, though, which is just gross when you think about it. It’s basically just sugar water at that point. But anyway... yeah, I don't think I've really lost interest in things. I still try to keep up with stuff.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different parts of your life, rather than mainly about the mortgage and work?

Um, worrying about other stuff? Not... not really, no. It's mostly just the house and the restaurant. I mean, the mortgage is the big thing. I keep trying to figure out if I should refinance, but the interest rates are just ridiculous right now. I saw on the news the other morning—well, I was actually watching the weather, because I needed to know if I should put a tarp over the firewood I bought. I got a half-cord from this guy off Craigslist, and he promised it was seasoned oak, but honestly, it feels kind of damp. You know how if you burn green wood, it creates all that creosote in the chimney? My uncle had a chimney fire back in like, 2008, because he never got it swept. The fire department had to come out, and they got water all over his living room rug. It was this really nice Persian rug, too. He tried to get it professionally cleaned, but it always smelled a little bit like wet dog after that. He didn't even have a dog, just a couple of parakeets. But yeah, no, I don't really worry about a bunch of different things. Just the main stuff, mostly.
In addition to feeling depressed and guilty, have you been feeling persistently nervous, tense, or on edge?

Um... nervous or tense? No, I wouldn't say I feel like that. I mean, I don't feel on edge or anything. I just feel so down and... bad about myself, mostly. I actually tried to relax the other night by taking a bath. I bought these bath bombs from this little shop downtown, the one right next to the bakery that sells those amazing almond croissants. Have you ever had one? They have this powdered sugar on top that just gets everywhere, it's impossible to eat in the car. I tried once and ended up looking like a ghost. Anyway, the bath bomb was supposed to be lavender and chamomile, for stress relief, you know? But when I dropped it in the water, it just fizzed for a second and then turned the whole tub this weird swampy green color. It looked like algae. It reminded me of this pond behind my middle school that always smelled like sulfur in the summer. We used to catch frogs back there until they put up a chain-link fence. I don't even know why they fenced it off, maybe someone complained about the smell. But yeah, no, I'm not really feeling tense or nervous. Just the other stuff.
Did these depressed and guilty feelings begin within three months of taking on the mortgage or having problems at work?

Um, within three months? I don't really think it lined up like that. I'm not totally sure when it all started, honestly. The mortgage took forever to close anyway. I remember sitting at the title company's office to sign everything, and the notary had this enormous jar of jelly beans on her desk. They were all the weird flavors, though, like buttered popcorn and licorice. Who actually eats the licorice ones? They taste like cough medicine. My grandma used to keep black licorice in her purse, the kind that comes in those little twisted wrappers. She'd give them to us at church to keep us quiet, but it just made me thirsty. And you couldn't get up to get water because the aisles were so narrow in that old building. They had these really beautiful stained glass windows, though, especially when the sun hit them in the morning. But anyway... yeah, I don't really know if the sad feelings started exactly right after the house or the restaurant stuff. I just haven't been keeping track of the months like that.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep during this period?

Um, sleep? No, I don't think my sleep has changed much. I mean, I sleep okay, I guess. I did get this new pillow recently, though. It's one of those memory foam ones that's supposed to stay cool all night. I saw an ad for it on Instagram, and it looked really comfortable. The guy in the commercial was sleeping on a block of ice or something to prove a point. I don't know how they film those things. Like, does the actor actually sleep, or do they just pretend? I took a drama class in community college, and we had to do this exercise where we pretended to be different animals. I was a sloth, which was actually pretty hard because you have to move so slow. My arms got really tired. The teacher was this guy who always wore turtlenecks, even when it was like 80 degrees outside. He said it protected his vocal cords. I always wondered if he was just hiding a bad tattoo on his neck or something. But yeah, my sleep is pretty much the same as always. Nothing really different there.
Have you had thoughts of ending your life or hurting yourself?

Um, thoughts of hurting myself? No, I don't... I don't have a plan to do anything like that. But, um, sometimes when I'm just lying there in bed, especially right before I have to get up for an early shift at the restaurant... I just think it would be so much easier if I didn't wake up. Like, if I just didn't have to face the day and keep failing at everything, you know? The early shifts are the worst anyway. You have to be there before the sun is even up, and the kitchen always smells like old grease and bleach first thing in the morning. The bleach smell is so strong it kind of burns your nose. My mom used to clean our whole house with bleach every Saturday morning. You couldn't even walk into the bathroom without your eyes watering. She'd put on these bright yellow rubber gloves, the kind that go all the way up to your elbows. I bought a pair like that once to wash my car, but they melted in the trunk during the summer. I didn't realize how hot it gets in there. It completely ruined the upholstery on the spare tire. But yeah, I don't want to hurt myself or anything. Just... sometimes I wish I could just stop trying.
When you think back to when your mortgage closed, were you already feeling depressed at that time, or did those feelings begin afterward?

Um, when the mortgage closed? Let me think... well, I guess I've been feeling this way, like, really down and guilty about everything, for about a year and two months now. So, whatever that lines up with. A year and two months is actually how long I had my first car, this beat-up old Honda Civic. It was silver, but the paint on the hood was peeling off in these big flakes that looked like potato chips. I tried to fix it myself with some spray paint I got at the hardware store, but the color didn't match at all. It looked like a patchwork quilt. The guy at the hardware store said it was an exact match, but he was wearing these really thick glasses, so maybe he just couldn't see it right. He had a pet parrot in the store, too, which was so weird. It would squawk every time someone walked through the door. I wonder if parrots ever get headaches from being so loud all the time. Like, they don't have earplugs or anything. But anyway... yeah, it's been about a year and two months of feeling like this, so I guess it was happening around the same time as the mortgage stuff.
Over the past year, on how many days in a typical week have you felt depressed or down?

Um, how many days a week? I don't know... I'm not really sure how to count them. It just kind of blends together, honestly. Like, I don't really keep track of the days anymore. Keeping track of days is actually really hard when you work in a restaurant, because your schedule is always changing. Sometimes you work a Tuesday morning, and then a Thursday night, and then a double on Sunday. Sunday doubles are the worst, especially when the church crowd comes in. They always want everything modified, like "dressing on the side" or "no croutons," but then they complain that the salad looks small. One time, this lady brought her own salad dressing in a little Tupperware container. It looked like ranch, but it had these weird green flecks in it. I thought maybe it was dill, but then she said it was some kind of algae supplement she bought online. Algae! Like, what fish eat. I don't know why anyone would want to eat fish food on purpose. I had a goldfish once when I was a kid, won it at a carnival by throwing a ping-pong ball into a bowl. It only lived for three days, though. I think I overfed it. Or maybe it was the tap water. But yeah, I don't really know how many days a week I feel down. It's just... hard to say exactly.
During this period, have you had noticeably less energy than usual?

Um, energy? I don't... I haven't really noticed a difference, I guess. I mean, I'm always tired, but I don't know if it's less than usual. Usually, I just drink a lot of coffee to get through the shift. We have this huge industrial coffee maker at the restaurant, the kind that brews a whole pot in like two minutes. It's so loud, it sounds like an airplane taking off when it steams. Speaking of airplanes, I've always wanted to take a trip somewhere, like maybe to the beach. I haven't been to the ocean since I was a kid. The sand always gets everywhere, though. You find it in your shoes for weeks afterward. I remember finding a tiny seashell in my sneaker once, and it was perfectly intact. It was white with these little pink stripes. I put it on my windowsill, but my cat knocked it off and it shattered. He's always knocking things off shelves. Cats are so weird like that, they just look at you right in the eye while they push a glass off the table. But anyway, yeah, I haven't really noticed if my energy is less or not. I'm just tired a lot.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite during this period?

Um, my appetite? It's kind of been all over the place, really. Like, some weeks I barely even touch the staff meal before my shift. And then other nights, I get home from work and just eat whatever I can find in the kitchen, just to feel... I don't know, settled, I guess. It's weird because the staff meals are usually pretty good. The head chef, Marco, he makes this incredible baked ziti on Thursdays. He uses like three different kinds of cheese. He says the secret is a little bit of nutmeg in the ricotta, which sounds crazy for pasta, but it actually works. Nutmeg always reminds me of eggnog, though. I tried making eggnog from scratch one Christmas, but I think I scrambled the eggs by mistake because the milk was too hot. It ended up tasting like sweet breakfast food in a glass. I poured it down the sink, and the disposal made this awful grinding noise. Disposals are terrifying if you think about it. Just blades spinning around in the dark. I always use a wooden spoon to push stuff down there, just in case. But yeah, my eating is just really unpredictable lately, either nothing at all or everything in sight.
On most days, do you feel depressed or down for much of the day?

Um, yeah, I guess so. Most days there's just this... this heavy, empty feeling right here in my chest. It's like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Carrying plates, refilling waters, smiling at the tables because I'm supposed to, not because I actually feel anything good. Smiling is a big part of the job. They always tell us in training, "Service with a smile," like it's some kind of magic spell that makes the food taste better. I had this one manager, Greg, who used to stand by the kitchen doors and literally tell us to show our teeth before we walked out onto the floor. Greg was intense. He drove this bright yellow sports car that he parked way out in the back of the lot so no one would scratch it. But then one day, a seagull dropped a half-eaten clam right on the hood and it chipped the paint anyway. Seagulls are ruthless. They hang out by the dumpsters out back and they're huge, like the size of small dogs. I saw one fly off with an entire slice of pepperoni pizza once. Just swooped down and took it right out of the box. But yeah, most of the day, it's just that heavy feeling, like I'm just pretending to be there while I'm working.
During this period, have you had trouble concentrating or making decisions, such as when reading, working, or handling everyday tasks?

Um, yeah, I've definitely noticed that. Especially at work. I’m having a lot of trouble keeping numbers straight on the POS and the inventory sheets lately. I’ll just stand there and stare at the screen, knowing I’ve done this for years, but totally not trusting what I just entered. It's frustrating. And those POS screens are always so smudged anyway. Everyone is always poking at them with greasy fingers after running plates of fries or whatever. I try to use hand sanitizer after I touch it, but the stuff management buys for us smells awful. It smells exactly like this really cheap tequila I drank back in college. We used to have these parties in my dorm, and someone would always bring a giant plastic bottle of it. I can't even look at tequila now without feeling a little sick. One time, my roommate tried to make margaritas in our blender, but he didn't put the lid on tight, and it sprayed green slush all over the acoustic ceiling tiles. We had to scrub it off with our toothbrushes before the RA did room inspections. Toothbrushes are actually really great for cleaning little crevices, like bathroom grout. I saw a video about that once, where this guy cleaned his whole shower with one. But, um... yeah, I just end up staring at the POS screen, second-guessing every single button I press.

I always wondered if he was just hiding a bad tattoo on his neck or something. But yeah, my sleep is pretty much the same as always. Nothing really different there.

doctor.intent: Assess for suicidal ideation as a key depressive symptom and immediate safety concern.
doctor.question: Have you had thoughts of ending your life or hurting yourself?

target_item.name: Death_Suicide
target_item.manifestation: I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but when I’m lying awake before an early shift I sometimes think it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up and didn’t have to keep failing at everything.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I have had thoughts of ending my life or hurting myself, which directly matches the Death_Suicide symptom in my profile.

patient.answer: Um, thoughts of hurting myself? No, I don't... I don't have a plan to do anything like that. But, um, sometimes when I'm just lying there in bed, especially right before I have to get up for an early shift at the restaurant... I just think it would be so much easier if I didn't wake up. Like, if I just didn't have to face the day and keep failing at everything, you know? The early shifts are the worst anyway. You have to be there before the sun is even up, and the kitchen always smells like old grease and bleach first thing in the morning. The bleach smell is so strong it kind of burns your nose. My mom used to clean our whole house with bleach every Saturday morning. You couldn't even walk into the bathroom without your eyes watering. She'd put on these bright yellow rubber gloves, the kind that go all the way up to your elbows. I bought a pair like that once to wash my car, but they melted in the trunk during the summer. I didn't realize how hot it gets in there. It completely ruined the upholstery on the spare tire. But yeah, I don't want to hurt myself or anything. Just... sometimes I wish I could just stop trying.

inference.note: Persistent depressed mood, guilt, worthlessness, and passive death wishes for 14 months raise consideration of persistent depressive disorder (F34.1); insufficient symptoms and unclear stressor timing prevent narrowing further.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the depressive symptoms began in temporal response to the mortgage-related stressor, which helps distinguish adjustment disorder from a primary depressive disorder.
doctor.question: When you think back to when your mortgage closed, were you already feeling depressed at that time, or did those feelings begin afterward?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The depressed, guilty periods have been present for about 1 year and 2 months of this whole time.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the timeline and onset of the depressed feelings in relation to the mortgage closing, which corresponds to the duration of the depressive episode.

patient.answer: Um, when the mortgage closed? Let me think... well, I guess I've been feeling this way, like, really down and guilty about everything, for about a year and two months now. So, whatever that lines up with. A year and two months is actually how long I had my first car, this beat-up old Honda Civic. It was silver, but the paint on the hood was peeling off in these big flakes that looked like potato chips. I tried to fix it myself with some spray paint I got at the hardware store, but the color didn't match at all. It looked like a patchwork quilt. The guy at the hardware store said it was an exact match, but he was wearing these really thick glasses, so maybe he just couldn't see it right. He had a pet parrot in the store, too, which was so weird. It would squawk every time someone walked through the door. I wonder if parrots ever get headaches from being so loud all the time. Like, they don't have earplugs or anything. But anyway... yeah, it's been about a year and two months of feeling like this, so I guess it was happening around the same time as the mortgage stuff.

inference.note: No clear symptom-count evidence for a major depressive episode; preserved interest and sleep make F32.9 less definitive. The 14-month duration is below the 2-year threshold for F34.1, and onset relative to stressors remains unclear for F43.21.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressed mood is persistent enough to support a depressive disorder rather than episodic or stress-related symptoms.
doctor.question: Over the past year, on how many days in a typical week have you felt depressed or down?

patient.answer: Um, how many days a week? I don't know... I'm not really sure how to count them. It just kind of blends together, honestly. Like, I don't really keep track of the days anymore. Keeping track of days is actually really hard when you work in a restaurant, because your schedule is always changing. Sometimes you work a Tuesday morning, and then a Thursday night, and then a double on Sunday. Sunday doubles are the worst, especially when the church crowd comes in. They always want everything modified, like "dressing on the side" or "no croutons," but then they complain that the salad looks small. One time, this lady brought her own salad dressing in a little Tupperware container. It looked like ranch, but it had these weird green flecks in it. I thought maybe it was dill, but then she said it was some kind of algae supplement she bought online. Algae! Like, what fish eat. I don't know why anyone would want to eat fish food on purpose. I had a goldfish once when I was a kid, won it at a carnival by throwing a ping-pong ball into a bowl. It only lived for three days, though. I think I overfed it. Or maybe it was the tap water. But yeah, I don't really know how many days a week I feel down. It's just... hard to say exactly.

inference.note: Persistent depressive disorder (F34.1) is less likely because symptoms have lasted about 14 months, below the 2-year duration threshold. The patient reports depressed mood, guilt, worthlessness, and passive death wishes but insufficient additional symptoms to establish a major depressive episode; adjustment disorder remains possible, though timing relative to stressors is unclear.

doctor.intent: Assess for an additional major depressive episode symptom by determining whether the patient has experienced reduced energy.
doctor.question: During this period, have you had noticeably less energy than usual?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about fatigue or a noticeable loss of energy (often coded as S027), which is not included in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: Um, energy? I don't... I haven't really noticed a difference, I guess. I mean, I'm always tired, but I don't know if it's less than usual. Usually, I just drink a lot of coffee to get through the shift. We have this huge industrial coffee maker at the restaurant, the kind that brews a whole pot in like two minutes. It's so loud, it sounds like an airplane taking off when it steams. Speaking of airplanes, I've always wanted to take a trip somewhere, like maybe to the beach. I haven't been to the ocean since I was a kid. The sand always gets everywhere, though. You find it in your shoes for weeks afterward. I remember finding a tiny seashell in my sneaker once, and it was perfectly intact. It was white with these little pink stripes. I put it on my windowsill, but my cat knocked it off and it shattered. He's always knocking things off shelves. Cats are so weird like that, they just look at you right in the eye while they push a glass off the table. But anyway, yeah, I haven't really noticed if my energy is less or not. I'm just tired a lot.

inference.note: Passive death wishes and persistent guilt/depressed mood were clarified, but insufficient symptoms for a definitive major depressive episode; onset relative to stressors remains unclear, so both unspecified depressive disorder and adjustment disorder with depressed mood remain possible.

doctor.intent: Assess for another major depressive episode symptom to distinguish major depressive disorder from adjustment disorder
doctor.question: Have you noticed any change in your appetite during this period?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: My eating has been all over the place, where some weeks I barely touch staff meal and other nights I come home and eat whatever’s in the kitchen just to feel settled.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about changes in appetite, which directly matches the Weight_Appetite_Change symptom.

patient.answer: Um, my appetite? It's kind of been all over the place, really. Like, some weeks I barely even touch the staff meal before my shift. And then other nights, I get home from work and just eat whatever I can find in the kitchen, just to feel... I don't know, settled, I guess. It's weird because the staff meals are usually pretty good. The head chef, Marco, he makes this incredible baked ziti on Thursdays. He uses like three different kinds of cheese. He says the secret is a little bit of nutmeg in the ricotta, which sounds crazy for pasta, but it actually works. Nutmeg always reminds me of eggnog, though. I tried making eggnog from scratch one Christmas, but I think I scrambled the eggs by mistake because the milk was too hot. It ended up tasting like sweet breakfast food in a glass. I poured it down the sink, and the disposal made this awful grinding noise. Disposals are terrifying if you think about it. Just blades spinning around in the dark. I always use a wooden spoon to push stuff down there, just in case. But yeah, my eating is just really unpredictable lately, either nothing at all or everything in sight.

doctor.intent: Determine whether depressed mood is persistent and frequent enough to support a major depressive episode.
doctor.question: On most days, do you feel depressed or down for much of the day?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most days there’s this heavy, empty feeling in my chest, like I’m going through the motions carrying plates and smiling because I’m supposed to, not because I feel anything good.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about feeling depressed or down for much of the day, which maps to the Depressed Mood symptom.

patient.answer: Um, yeah, I guess so. Most days there's just this... this heavy, empty feeling right here in my chest. It's like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Carrying plates, refilling waters, smiling at the tables because I'm supposed to, not because I actually feel anything good. Smiling is a big part of the job. They always tell us in training, "Service with a smile," like it's some kind of magic spell that makes the food taste better. I had this one manager, Greg, who used to stand by the kitchen doors and literally tell us to show our teeth before we walked out onto the floor. Greg was intense. He drove this bright yellow sports car that he parked way out in the back of the lot so no one would scratch it. But then one day, a seagull dropped a half-eaten clam right on the hood and it chipped the paint anyway. Seagulls are ruthless. They hang out by the dumpsters out back and they're huge, like the size of small dogs. I saw one fly off with an entire slice of pepperoni pizza once. Just swooped down and took it right out of the box. But yeah, most of the day, it's just that heavy feeling, like I'm just pretending to be there while I'm working.

inference.note: This turn adds persistent depressed mood, appetite disturbance, guilt/worthlessness, and passive death wishes, supporting a depressive disorder; timing relative to the stressors remains unclear, so adjustment disorder remains possible.

doctor.intent: Assess for impaired concentration, which would help determine whether full major depressive episode criteria are met
doctor.question: During this period, have you had trouble concentrating or making decisions, such as when reading, working, or handling everyday tasks?

target_item.name: Diminished_Thinking
target_item.manifestation: I’m having trouble keeping numbers straight on the POS and inventory sheets, and I’ll stare at the screen knowing I’ve done this for years but not trusting what I just entered.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about trouble concentrating or making decisions, which maps to the Diminished_Thinking symptom in my profile.

patient.answer: Um, yeah, I've definitely noticed that. Especially at work. I’m having a lot of trouble keeping numbers straight on the POS and the inventory sheets lately. I’ll just stand there and stare at the screen, knowing I’ve done this for years, but totally not trusting what I just entered. It's frustrating. And those POS screens are always so smudged anyway. Everyone is always poking at them with greasy fingers after running plates of fries or whatever. I try to use hand sanitizer after I touch it, but the stuff management buys for us smells awful. It smells exactly like this really cheap tequila I drank back in college. We used to have these parties in my dorm, and someone would always bring a giant plastic bottle of it. I can't even look at tequila now without feeling a little sick. One time, my roommate tried to make margaritas in our blender, but he didn't put the lid on tight, and it sprayed green slush all over the acoustic ceiling tiles. We had to scrub it off with our toothbrushes before the RA did room inspections. Toothbrushes are actually really great for cleaning little crevices, like bathroom grout. I saw a video about that once, where this guy cleaned his whole shower with one. But, um... yeah, I just end up staring at the POS screen, second-guessing every single button I press.

inference.note: The patient now meets criteria for a moderate major depressive episode: persistent depressed mood, excessive guilt/worthlessness, appetite disturbance, impaired concentration, and passive thoughts of death with functional impairment. Adjustment disorder is less likely given unclear temporal linkage and symptoms meeting full depressive-episode criteria.
